newsitem.title: UK: No more AN-124s to be built, says Antonov agent.
newsitem.headline: No more AN-124s to be built, says Antonov agent.

text.p: It is unlikely that any further models of the Antonov AN-124, the world's biggest commercially-used freighter aircraft, will ever be built, said Antonov Design Bureau's (ADB) worldwide management agent.
Chris Foyle, chairman of the management company, UK-based Air Foyle, said that there were only 20 140-tonne capacity AN-124s in international commercial use, along with 30 military versions.
"There are two production sites and the one at Kiev, Ukraine, is not building any more AN-124s." Foyle told Reuters.
"The other one, at Ulyanovsk - home of Volga-Dnepr, the other major commercial AN-124 owner along with ADP - may be about to stop producing this aircraft," he said.

The Ulyanovsk plant was switching emphasis to producing the Tupolev Tu-204 - "the Russian equivalent of the Boeing 757" - and would therefore have little or no time to devote to further AN-124 manufacture, he added.
